title: Moving to Columbia TN: A Guide for Buyers Relocating
description: Moving to Columbia TN? See current Maury County market data, tax and school basics, commute notes and steps for Nashville or out-of-state buyers.
body:
Moving to Columbia TN means buying in Maury County. County services, property taxes and public schools all run through local offices there, so it helps to know who to call before you fall for a house.

This guide covers what the current numbers show, what to check address by address, and the steps that matter most if you are coming from Nashville or from out of state.

## What the Columbia numbers show right now

{{img:0}}

According to Redfin (rolling 3 months, data as of 2026-10-31), Columbia's median sale price is $354,753, down 1.4% from a year earlier. Median days on market is 75, the average sale-to-list ratio is 96.8%, and there are 450 active listings.

Redfin also reports 5.0 months of supply for Columbia. Months of supply is how long it would take to sell every active listing at the current pace of sales. Under 4 months favors sellers, 4 to 6 months is balanced, and over 6 months favors buyers. At 5.0, Columbia sits in the balanced range on that measure.

Other readings are not identical. Zillow's Market Temperature Index for Columbia is 32 (Zillow Research, as of 2026-10-31), and the overall rating I have for Columbia leans toward buyers. The trend is heating, with the Zillow index up 11 over three months. Taken together, that is a mixed picture, and it can shift. Individual homes and price ranges can behave differently from the city as a whole.

For comparison, Redfin shows the Nashville metro area for the 4 weeks ending 2026-11-08 with a median sale price of $467,332, median days on market of 69, a sale-to-list ratio of 97.7%, 5.9 months of supply and 2,232 homes sold. The time windows differ between the two sets of figures, so treat them as context, not a precise side-by-side. You can follow more local figures on the [Market data for the I-65 corridor](/market-data) page.

On financing, Freddie Mac via FRED shows the 30-year fixed mortgage rate at 7.11% for the week of 2026-11-12. Nobody can reliably predict where rates go next. If you want to see how a rate changes a payment, try the [Mortgage calculator](/mortgage-calculator) with your own numbers.

## Property taxes and schools depend on the address

For the 2025 tax year, the combined property tax rate inside Columbia city limits is $2.7351 per $100 of assessed value, made up of $1.91 for the county and $0.8251 for the city (Maury County community profile, citing the Tennessee Comptroller, Division of Property Assessments). Tennessee assesses residential property at 25% of appraised value.

As a simple illustration only, a home appraised at $100,000 would be assessed at $25,000. At the combined city rate, that works out to about $684 a year. Your actual bill depends on the home's appraisal and its exact location.

These are the 2025 rates, the latest I found. Maury County is in a 2026 reappraisal year, when rates are reset, so the 2026 rates may be lower. Confirm current figures with the Maury County Trustee through [Maury County Government](https://www.maurycounty-tn.gov), and see [City of Columbia](https://www.columbiatn.gov) for city information. For a wider budget view, there is a page on [Columbia cost of living](/columbia/cost-of-living).

Schools work the same way. Columbia addresses are zoned through Maury County Public Schools, and the most reliable way to find the zoned school for a home is the district's own lookup tool at [Maury County Public Schools](https://www.mauryk12.org). Whether a home is close to the Duck River or elsewhere in Maury County, verify the school and the tax details for that specific address. Our page on [Columbia school districts](/columbia/schools) is another place to start.

If you are also looking at Spring Hill, note that it includes parts of both Williamson and Maury counties, so county services, schools and taxes can differ by address. See [Columbia vs Spring Hill](/columbia/columbia-vs-spring-hill) for that comparison.

## Check the commute yourself

{{img:1}}

The U.S. Census Bureau's American Community Survey (5-year estimates, 2020 to 2024) shows a mean travel time to work of 28 minutes for Columbia. That is an average across many trips, not a number for your route or your hours.

If you will keep a job elsewhere, drive the route at the times you would actually travel. TDOT's [TDOT SmartWay traffic](https://smartway.tn.gov) site shows current conditions. More background is on the [Columbia commute times](/columbia/commute) page.

The same Census data shows a median gross rent of $1,197 per month in Columbia, and 63.3% of homes are owner-occupied. If you are weighing renting against buying, compare the full monthly cost of buying (payment, taxes, insurance, maintenance) with the cost of renting a comparable home, and think about how long you expect to stay.

## Steps for buyers coming from Nashville or out of state

**Get pre-approved, not just pre-qualified.** A pre-qualification is a quick estimate based on what you tell a lender. A pre-approval means the lender has reviewed your documents and credit. Even then, a pre-approval letter is not a final loan commitment. Final approval depends on the appraisal, underwriting and your finances staying the same until closing.

**Compare lenders.** The CFPB encourages borrowers to get Loan Estimates from more than one lender, because rates and fees can differ. The Loan Estimate is a standard three-page form, so you can compare them side by side. You choose your own lender. You can also ask any lender whether they take part in Tennessee Housing Development Agency (THDA) loan programs.

**Protect your credit and your money.** Avoid opening new credit, financing furniture or changing jobs from the time you apply through closing. Verify wire instructions by phone using a number you already trust, and never rely on emailed wire instructions.

**Plan inspections.** Radon testing, a sewer scope and a termite inspection are common add-ons to a standard home inspection. Termite and wood-destroying organism (WDO) inspections are commonly requested by buyers and lenders in Tennessee. Tennessee sellers also complete the residential property condition disclosure (or exemption), and the lead-based paint disclosure applies to homes built before 1978.

**Line up the move.** Request quotes from at least 3 licensed moving companies and book early for month-end dates. Cancel homeowner's insurance on a sold home only after closing is confirmed. The [Free moving checklists](/checklists) can help you keep the pieces organized.

## Costs to plan for

Closing costs typically run 2 to 4 percent of the purchase price, plus earnest money and moving costs. Private mortgage insurance is typically required on conventional loans when the down payment is under 20 percent. FHA loans allow a down payment as low as 3.5 percent, and VA loans typically require no down payment and no monthly mortgage insurance, though a funding fee may apply. A lender can tell you what fits your situation.

Don't forget utilities. Electric service in the area is handled through providers such as [Middle Tennessee Electric](https://www.mte.com), so confirm who serves a specific address before you set up service.

## Talk it through

I work with buyers moving from Nashville and from out of state, and I am happy to talk through what you are weighing. If you fill out the [Get matched with homes](/buy#form) form, I will schedule a call and we will be talking within the next 48 hours. You can also reach me directly through [Contact Scott](/contact).

Scott Davis, REALTOR®, RE/MAX Choice Properties

faq.q: Is Columbia, TN a buyer's market?
faq.a: The signals are mixed. Redfin shows 5.0 months of supply as of 2026-10-31, which falls in the balanced range of 4 to 6 months, while Zillow's Market Temperature Index of 32 leans toward buyers and is trending up. Conditions can differ by price range and home.

faq.q: How do I find the school zone for a Columbia home?
faq.a: Columbia addresses are zoned through Maury County Public Schools. The most reliable way to confirm the zoned school is the district's own lookup tool, using the home's exact address.
